text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture)

Based on your history of forceful retching after heavy alcohol consumption, followed immediately by severe chest pain and choking, I suspect a tear in your esophagus. Given the severity of your symptoms and inability to communicate, I am proceeding with this diagnosis immediately. Please ensure emergency surgical intervention is prepared.
